subject: physics
title: E.m.f. and internal resistance
key_idea: The e.m.f. of a source is the energy it gives to each coulomb of charge driven round a complete circuit. The source has internal resistance, so some of that energy is lost inside it. The terminal p.d. is the e.m.f. minus the lost volts: V = E − Ir.

blocks.text: E.m.f. and p.d. are both measured in volts, but they describe energy changing in opposite directions.

items.meaning: The energy transferred to each unit of charge by a source, as it drives the charge round a complete circuit. Energy changes from chemical (or other) to electrical.
The energy transferred from electrical to other forms per unit charge, as charge moves through a component.

blocks.label: E.m.f.
where: W = energy given to the charge by the source (J)

items: E.m.f. is energy **gained** by the charge in the source. p.d. is energy **lost** by the charge in a component.
The symbol E here is the e.m.f. It is not energy, electric field strength or Young modulus, which share the same letter. Some books use ε.
An e.m.f. is measured with a high-resistance voltmeter across the source when no current is drawn.
E.m.f. is energy supplied per unit charge by the source.
p.d. is energy transferred per unit charge in a component.

blocks.text: Every real source has resistance inside it. Charge flowing through the source transfers some energy there as well as in the circuit.

items.meaning: The resistance of the source itself, which transfers energy inside the source as thermal energy.
The p.d. across the terminals of the source when it supplies a current. It is the p.d. across the external circuit.
The p.d. across the internal resistance, equal to Ir. Energy per unit charge wasted inside the source.

blocks.label: Current in a circuit with internal resistance
where: R = resistance of the external circuit (Ω)
R + r = total resistance of the circuit (Ω)

items.text: By conservation of energy, E = IR + Ir, because the e.m.f. drives the current through both resistances.
V = IR is the p.d. across the external circuit, so E = V + Ir.

diagram.alt: Change the e.m.f., internal resistance and load resistance to see the current, terminal p.d. and lost volts.

items: With no current, there are no lost volts, so the terminal p.d. equals the e.m.f.
As the current increases, Ir increases, so the terminal p.d. falls.
A low external resistance draws a large current and a large drop in terminal p.d.
A source with a large internal resistance cannot supply a large current.
V = E − Ir, and E = I(R + r).
Terminal p.d. equals e.m.f. only when no current is drawn.
Lost volts Ir increase with current.

blocks.text: Vary the current in a cell and measure how its terminal p.d. changes.

items.text: Connect the cell in series with an ammeter and a variable resistor. Connect a voltmeter across the cell terminals.
Change the variable resistor to alter the current. Record V and I for at least six settings.
Switch the circuit off between readings so the cell does not run down or warm up.
Plot V (y-axis) against I (x-axis). Draw a line of best fit.

diagram.alt: Graph of terminal p.d. against current for a cell. It is a straight line sloping down. The y-intercept is the e.m.f. and the gradient is minus the internal resistance.

items: Compare V = E − Ir with y = c + mx: the **y-intercept** is E.
The **gradient** is −r, so r is the size of the gradient.
The x-intercept is the short-circuit current, E / r.
Plot V against I: intercept = E, gradient = −r.
Switch off between readings to avoid heating the cell.

checks.q: State the difference between e.m.f. and potential difference in terms of energy.
checks.a: E.m.f. is the energy transferred to each unit of charge by the source, from chemical to electrical. p.d. is the energy transferred from electrical to other forms per unit charge in a component.

checks.q: A cell of e.m.f. 1.50 V and internal resistance 0.60 Ω is connected to a 2.4 Ω resistor. Calculate the current and the terminal p.d.
A graph of terminal p.d. against current for a cell is a straight line through (0, 1.6 V) and (2.0 A, 1.2 V). Find the e.m.f. and internal resistance.
checks.a: E is the y-intercept: 1.6 V. r is minus the gradient: (1.6 − 1.2) ÷ 2.0 = 0.20 Ω.
